en: Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor pertaining to the stages of training (na-kusala-na-sekkha), a wholesome state pertaining to the stages of training (kusala-sekkha) arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are six; ... [and so on] ... under repetition-condition (*āsevana*) there are three; ... [and so on] ... under result-condition (*vipāka*) there are three; ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*) there are six.

Conditioned by a state that is neither wholesome nor pertaining to the stages of training, an indeterminate state pertaining to the stages beyond training (*abyākata-asekkha*) arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three; ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance-condition there are three.

Dependent upon a state that is neither wholesome nor pertaining to the stages of training, an indeterminate state that pertains neither to the stages of training nor to those beyond training (*abyākata-neva-sekkha-nāsekkha*) [arises].

It arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Five in the case of the root; five in the case of the predominance [condition] ... three in the case of the result ... five in the case of non-disappearance.
